prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry specific to the field of electrical engineering
Extensive knowledge of chemistry and physics, but also of electricity

learning_outcomes.text: Proper implementation of specific fundamental knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry, in the field of electrical engineering
Use of fundamental knowledge of electrotechnics
Diagnosis, troubleshooting and maintenance of electrical systems and components
Identification of the objectives to be achieved, available resources, conditions to complete them, working stages, working times, associated deadlines and risks
Identification of the roles and responsibilities in a multidisciplinary team and use of relationship and effective working techniques in the team

Effective use of information and communication sources and assisted professional training (Internet portals, specialized software applications, databases, online courses etc.) both in Romanian and in a foreign language.
The course aims to present energy phenomena in terms of applications in technology to students in the engineering department, both in electrical engineering.
To present in a unitary framework, natural phenomena and resources as well as some applications in this field, necessary for knowing how to design and apply them.
Evaluate errors in experimental determinations performed.
Better collaboration with colleagues in team work.

syllabus_topics: The energy of the seas and oceans
The current stage of installation of nuclear power plants
Speed regulation and tracing of operating characteristics (both current - voltage and current - resistance) to 6-12 V motors powered by a 1.5 W solar panel, and filtering the supply voltage
Heating of domestic hot water with the help of solar panels
Conversion of wind energy into electricity. Valslr PP-H HTM.DN 110. EN1451
assessment_rules: Minimum performance standard offers the formation of skills in the energy field and highlights both the phenomena and methods of conversion of solar, wind, nuclear, geothermal, etc. into electricity.
